## Body

## Security verdict: BLOCK

PR #196, exact head `a5cea92a3414e596a2ed4d655d11690faa66b4cc`.

The complete five-file diff and shell/plist serialization boundaries were source-reviewed. The bounce assignment is shell-safe, but hostile PIJ_IDLE_NUDGE content can escape its plist string and change launchd configuration.

| # | Severity | File | Lines | Vulnerability | Confidence |
|---|----------|------|-------|---------------|------------|
| 1 | 🟡 MEDIUM | justfile | 682 | Unescaped PIJ_IDLE_NUDGE XML can inject a top-level launchd Program key | 9/10 |

### S196-001: variable data becomes launch configuration

The unquoted heredoc interpolates the raw variable into `<string>${PIJ_IDLE_NUDGE-1}</string>`. There is no XML encoding or boolean normalization before writing the LaunchAgent.

An adversarial value can close the string and EnvironmentVariables dictionary, add a top-level Program key, and reopen a dictionary to leave balanced XML. For example, a value naming the harmless `/bin/echo` executable demonstrates the structural escape:

```text
0</string></dict><key>Program</key><string>/bin/echo</string><key>EnvironmentVariables</key><dict><key>PIJ_IDLE_NUDGE</key><string>0
```

This value was not executed. The launchd manual documents that Program selects the executable; ProgramArguments supplies argv and selects an executable only when Program is absent. Therefore retaining the original ProgramArguments does not neutralize the injected key. `plutil -lint` validates syntax, not authorized configuration.

Prerequisites are influence over PIJ_IDLE_NUDGE during the operator's rs-autostart invocation and, for arbitrary code execution, an accessible executable. Execution is in that GUI user's context. No remote entry point or privilege escalation was established.

Normalize this boolean to a literal 0/1 before plist generation, or serialize it with a proper plist string encoder.

### Other boundaries and proof

The bounce-rs environment assignment is double-quoted; embedded quotes/newlines and literal command-substitution text are data, not reevaluated shell syntax (`justfile:651`). No eval was found. The Rust daemon still defaults off and parses accepted values after launch; that downstream parser cannot protect an already-consumed launchd configuration.

Default/explicit-zero tests fake plutil and launchctl and do not establish hostile-value XML safety. No broader authentication/network control or C19/C21 disclosure was identified in the changes.

Independent executable-selection reference: https://keith.github.io/xcode-man-pages/launchd.plist.5.html (`Program`, `ProgramArguments`).

GitHub metadata and the independent remote pull ref agree on the full reviewed SHA; GitHub reports CLEAN. CI run `42531040882` and Delivers run `42531040878` both identify this SHA and success.

No local builds, tests, recipe/plist execution, daemon bounce, launchctl operation, credential reads or mutations were performed.
